doc.title: Jon Hendricks interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, October 18, 1995 [interview 1 of 2]

title: Leonard Feather, 'Learned Father'
summary: Hendricks praises Feather as a critic with credentials as a musician.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Critics, polls and the jazz press

blocks.x: Well on behalf of Hamilton College, it’s been a great, great pleasure having the poet laureate of jazz. There’s another one.

Leonard Feather. You know what we called Leonard? God rest his soul I loved him, he was a good friend of mine. But we called him “Learned Father.” Well you know why, because Leonard was the definitive jazz critic. You know most guys who play, take umbrage at being criticized — by being criticized by somebody that can’t play. Leonard wrote and recorded the first three tunes on Dinah Washington’s first album, and played piano on the date. So there you are. He has a right.
Right. He established himself, and then — © Hamilton College Jazz Archive -12-
He has bona fides. So when he criticizes, you are forced to pay attention.
